body.statement: Under \(H_\delta\), for every fixed potential-outcome schedule, every fixed treatment-indexed observation schedule, and every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), \(\Pr_w\{P_\delta(A)\le\alpha\}\le\alpha\). Consequently \(\Pr_w\{\delta\in\mathcal I_\alpha(A)\}\ge1-\alpha\).
body.justification: Pointwise domination of the infeasible oracle tail yields unconditional finite-sample size control despite treatment-dependent observation.
body.gap: General Fisher validity is known from Luo et al.; Li, Sheng, and Yu study worst-case completion under exchangeability and altered index tie-breaking; and Heng, Zhang, and Feng establish imputation-assisted randomization validity through re-imputation. None evaluates the equality-complete supplied-support Wilcoxon-midrank envelope stated here.
body.consumer: An analyst can report a finite-population exact confidence set without conditioning on the realized survivor set.
body.proof_tex:
Under the sharp additive null, define the fixed complete baseline vector
\[
b_i^\star=Y_i(0),\qquad i\in I.
\]
The fixed-potential-outcomes and fixed-observation-schedule assumptions make \(b^\star\) nonrandom under the sole assignment draw.  For every possible realization \(a\in\Omega\) and every observed label \(i\) under that realization, the sharp-null assumption gives
\[
Y_i(a_i)-\delta a_i=Y_i(0)=b_i^\star.
\]
Therefore \(b^\star\in\mathcal C_\delta(a)\) for every \(a\in\Omega\), even though \(M(a)\) may vary with \(a\).  Weak-order attainment and the definition of the robust p-value consequently imply the pointwise domination
\[
P_\delta(a)\ge p(a,b^\star),\qquad a\in\Omega.
\]

We next prove, rather than assume, super-uniformity of the oracle tail.  Let the distinct values of \(T(z,b^\star)\), in decreasing order, be \(t_1>\cdots>t_J\), and put
\[
\mu_j=\sum_{z\in\Omega}w_z\mathbf 1\{T(z,b^\star)=t_j\},
\qquad
c_j=\sum_{\ell=1}^j\mu_\ell.
\]
Positivity and normalization of the design weights give \(\mu_j>0\), \(c_j\) increasing, and \(c_J=1\).  If \(T(a,b^\star)=t_j\), the oracle-tail definition gives \(p(a,b^\star)=c_j\).  Hence, if \(j_\alpha=\max\{j:c_j\le\alpha\}\) exists,
\[
\Pr_w\{p(A,b^\star)\le\alpha\}
=\sum_{j=1}^{j_\alpha}\mu_j
=c_{j_\alpha}\le\alpha;
\]
if that set is empty, the probability is zero.  This calculation is valid for arbitrary positive weights and retains all statistic ties.

Pointwise domination yields the event inclusion
\[
\{P_\delta(A)\le\alpha\}
\subseteq
\{p(A,b^\star)\le\alpha\},
\]
so \(\Pr_w\{P_\delta(A)\le\alpha\}\le\alpha\).  Finally, by the definition \(\mathcal I_\alpha(A)=\{d:P_d(A)>\alpha\}\), at the true common effect \(\delta\),
\[
\{\delta\notin\mathcal I_\alpha(A)\}
=\{P_\delta(A)\le\alpha\}.
\]
Taking complements proves \(\Pr_w\{\delta\in\mathcal I_\alpha(A)\}\ge1-\alpha\).  No conditioning on the realized observation set has entered the argument.
